name: George Santos
role: US Representative for New York's 3rd district (2023); expelled from the House on December 1, 2023
summary: Santos, a Republican, ran for Congress in 2022 on crime, border security, cutting taxes and the cost of living, and aligned himself with Donald Trump. As a House member he cosponsored bills on gun rights, China and repealing the Inflation Reduction Act, and he was expelled after an ethics investigation and federal indictment over his biography and finances.

sources.title: George Santos
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.usedFor: Secondhand reports: 2022 abortion speech ('barbaric', compared to slavery), 'police brutality' remark, post-October 7 'police state' remark, vote against the Fiscal Responsibility Act (not mapped to a statement), career summary

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to repeal President Biden's healthcare and climate spending law (NY1). This is opposition to one federal health spending program; universal healthcare is not addressed directly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said his campaign focused on cutting taxes (Fox News) and introduced the SALT Relief Act to raise the state and local tax deduction cap from $10,000 to $50,000 (FOX 5). He did not address higher taxes on the wealthy directly, so the answer is a mild disagreement at low confidence.

limit-guns.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to make the AR-15 the national gun, a law-enforcement bill allowing concealed carry in school zones and national parks, and the Firearm Industry Non-Discrimination Act (NY1; Yahoo News). Cosponsorship shows support for these bills, not every reading of the statement.

empower-police-military.rationale: Called for funding for the NYPD and said the state faces a 'crime wave crisis' (Fox News). The statement is about police and military, and his record covers police funding; no military position was found.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reported by Wikipedia as calling abortion 'barbaric' and comparing it to slavery in a 2022 speech (secondhand). After the Dobbs decision he said it gave power back to New York's people (Fox News), which is about who decides rather than a stated view on legality. Low confidence.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Campaigned on strengthening border security (Fox News), cosponsored a bill to remove legal obstacles to a border wall (NY1), and offered an amendment to re-establish a Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement Office (NBC News). These do not state a target for immigration levels.

open-borders.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to remove legal obstacles to building a border wall (NY1) and campaigned on border security (Fox News). These show opposition to open borders, but he did not address an eventual open border directly.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to repeal President Biden's healthcare and climate spending law, the Inflation Reduction Act (NY1). That is opposition to one federal climate program, not to drastic action in general.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Reported by Wikipedia as calling police brutality a 'made-up concept.' Secondhand and only about police, so the disagreement is low confidence.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Reported by Wikipedia as saying after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, 'I don't care if we go into a police state for a couple of months.' The remark is secondhand and does not say which legal protections it would suspend.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment that would limit pay for members of Congress (NBC News). The exact pay limit is not reported, so this is only a partial match.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Backed the Equality and Fiscal Accountability Act of 2023, which would stop federal aid to countries that criminalize homosexuality, and said of such countries: 'you need to knock that crap out' (Long Island Herald).

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to bar individuals born male from women's and girls' school sports (NY1). This covers only sports, and the broader legal recognition question is not addressed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment that would limit congressional pay and reduce the national debt (NBC News). The text of the amendment is not reported, so whether it would bind borrowing is unclear.

close-ties-china.rationale: Introduced or cosponsored several China-focused bills, including the Defund the CCP on Campus Act of 2023 and a China-ties disclosure bill for colleges (NBC News; Yahoo News). NBC reports that 12 of his bills explicitly targeted China.

notes: Research was limited: WebSearch made 7 calls; the 6th and 7th returned the message: this session's web search budget is used up (a session-wide limit of 200 shared by every agent), and no searching was routed around it. Pages were read only where a search or Wikipedia link returned them. Not found: his House votes on Ukraine or Israel aid, his stated position on Social Security and Medicare, and the text of his 2022 abortion speech; those statements stay null. Wikipedia reports he voted against final passage of the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (one of 71 Republicans) and voted for the bills backed by House Republican leadership; the statement list has no matching position, so no answer was taken from these votes. The 2022 campaign platform items on energy independence and a flat tax appeared only in search snippets and were not opened, so they are not cited. Ideology is not inferred for this living person.
